'''Charles Herbert Clemens''' '''Jr.''' (born 15 August 1939)<ref>biographical information from ''American Men and trans of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004</ref> is an American mathematician specializing in complex [[algebraic geometry]].<ref name="utah">{{cite web|url=http://www.math.utah.edu/research/brochure/clemens2.pdf |title= Complex geometry, Herbert Clemens |publisher=math.utah.edu|access-date=2015-11-02}}</ref>

==Biography==
Clemens graduated from the [[College of the Holy Cross]] in [[Worcester, Massachusetts]], with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in mathematics in 1961. He then earned his [[Ph.D.]] in mathematics from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], under [[Phillip Griffiths]]. His doctoral dissertation was titled, ''Picard–Lefschetz Theorem for Families of Algebraic Varieties Acquiring Certain Singularities''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=19891}}</ref> In 1970, he became an assistant professor at [[Columbia University]] and went on to become an associate professor before leaving in 1975 to become an associate professor at the [[University of Utah]], where he became a full professor in 1976 and a Distinguished Professor in 2001.  In 2002, he left Utah to become a professor of mathematics and mathematics education at [[Ohio State University]].<ref name="msri">{{cite web|url=https://www.msri.org/people/8328 |title=Personal Profile of Mr. Herbert Clemens| publisher=MSRI|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref>

Clemens was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from September 1968 to March 1970 and from September 2001 to June 2003.<ref name="ias">{{cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/4222 |title=Clemens, Charles Herbert &#124; Institute for Advanced Study|publisher=ias.edu|access-date=2015-11-01}}</ref> He was an [[invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1976 at Vancouver and in 1986 at Berkeley and gave a talk ''Curves on higher dimensional complex projective manifolds''. For the academic year 1974–1975 he was a [[Sloan Fellow]].

In 1972 Clemens and Griffiths proved that a cubic [[three-fold]] is in general not a [[rational variety]], providing an example for three dimensions that unirationality does not imply rationality. In 1986 Clemens was an editor of the [[Pacific Journal of Mathematics]].

He married in 1983 and has three children.
